plain_english: Either you or the client can end the contract by giving a written 30‑day notice. When the contract ends, the client must pay you for any work you’ve already done, and you must give back any client materials within 15 days.
what_it_means_for_you: You can walk away with 30 days’ notice, but you must return client materials quickly and will only be paid for work done up to termination.
risk_reasons: Both parties have the same notice period, so the clause isn’t one‑sided
Payment is limited to services actually rendered, which is standard
The return‑material deadline is reasonable and does not impose harsh penalties
questions_to_ask: What counts as “services rendered” – does it include work in progress?
If the client delays payment after termination, what recourse do I have?
Can the 15‑day return period be extended if returning materials is impractical?
Are there any fees or penalties for terminating early that aren’t mentioned here?
evidence_quote: Either party may terminate this Agreement by providing 30 (thirty) days' written notice to the other party.
